docs.title: SpecForge ⚡
docs.text:
The Interactive API Client & Automated Contract Testing Engine for Python.

SpecForge is a modern, drop-in Python library that replaces Swagger UI with a beautiful, responsive API workspace and automatically discovers boundary vulnerabilities, missing whitespace stripping, and unhandled 500 server crashes directly against your endpoints.

docs.title: 1. Active Quality Gate, Not Just Passive Docs
docs.text: Traditional documentation tools like Swagger UI only show the "happy path" with mock examples. SpecForge algorithmically analyzes your schema constraints and executes targeted boundary fuzzing right in your browser or through the CLI.

docs.title: 2. "Zero 500s" Invariant
docs.text: Verifies that edge-case inputs (e.g. whitespace-only strings " ", empty values, off-by-one numbers, malformed emails) return clean client validation errors (422/400), never unhandled server exceptions (500).

docs.title: 3. One-Click Pytest Exporter
docs.text: Discovered edge cases and regression vulnerabilities can be instantly exported into commit-ready test_api_contracts.py files with standard @pytest.mark.parametrize matrices.

docs.title: 4. Existing Project Tests Discovery
docs.text: If your project already has test suites written in pytest or unittest, SpecForge can automatically index and display them in a dedicated Project Tests tab and link them directly to their corresponding API routes.

docs.title: 5. Zero Frontend Build Dependencies
docs.text: The interactive studio is fully compiled and inlined into the Python package. No Node.js, npm, or webpack setup is needed on your machine.

docs.title: ⚡ Installation in 10 Seconds
docs.text:
pip install specforge-api

With framework extras:

FastAPIFlaskAll Frameworks & CLI 
pip install "specforge-api[fastapi]"

pip install "specforge-api[flask]"

pip install "specforge-api[all]"

Ready to explore? Head over to the Quickstart Guide to mount SpecForge in 3 lines of code!

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: SpecForge comes with a built-in Command Line Interface (specforge) for working with OpenAPI specifications offline, spinning up mock studios, and running invariant test suites from your terminal.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The CLI requires the cli or all extra:

pip install "specforge-api[all]"

Verify installation: 

specforge --help

docs.title: specforge serve
docs.text:
Launches the standalone interactive studio for any OpenAPI YAML or JSON specification file:

# Serve local OpenAPI file
specforge serve openapi.yaml --port 8000

# Serve with custom studio title and theme
specforge serve spec.json --title "Customer API" --theme theme-2

docs.title: specforge test
docs.text:
Executes automated boundary and contract tests directly from your terminal against a live running API:

# Test all endpoints defined in openapi.yaml against target server
specforge test openapi.yaml --base-url http://localhost:8000

# Stop on first 500 error and print reproduction cURL command
specforge test openapi.yaml --base-url http://localhost:8000 --fail-fast

docs.title: specforge export
docs.text:
Exports synthesized boundary test cases for an OpenAPI spec into a pytest test file:

specforge export openapi.yaml --output tests/test_generated_contracts.py

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text: SpecForge is configured using the SpecForgeConfig dataclass or by passing keyword arguments directly to the framework adapters (SpecForge(app, ...)).

docs.title: Configuration Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description spec_url str "/openapi.json" Path or URL to the OpenAPI specification. path str "/docs" The HTTP route where the SpecForge studio will be served. title str "SpecForge - API Explorer & Quality Gate" Browser title displayed in the tab bar. theme str "theme-1" Initial UI color palette (theme-1: Indigo Slate, theme-2: Emerald Teal, theme-3: Midnight Dark, theme-4: Cobalt Blue). read_only bool False Disables sending requests or executing invariant tests from the browser. test_paths list[str] [] List of directory paths or test files to scan for existing tests. base_url str \| None None Default API target host when executing requests (defaults to current browser origin). hide_internal_models bool False Hides schemas prefixed with an underscore or tagged as internal.

docs.title: Example Usage with SpecForgeConfig
docs.text:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from specforge import SpecForge, SpecForgeConfig

app = FastAPI()

config = SpecForgeConfig(
    path="/api-docs",
    title="Core Platform Studio",
    theme="theme-2",
    test_paths=["tests/contract", "tests/unit"],
)

SpecForge(app, config=config)

docs.title: Quickstart Guide
docs.text: Get up and running with SpecForge in less than a minute.

docs.title: 1. Installation
docs.text:
Install SpecForge from PyPI:

pip install "specforge-api[all]"

docs.title: 2. Mount SpecForge in Your Application
docs.text:
FastAPIFlask 
from fastapi import FastAPI
from specforge import SpecForge

app = FastAPI(title="Store API", version="1.0.0")

# Mount SpecForge (automatically replaces /docs and auto-detects /openapi.json)
SpecForge(app)

@app.post("/items")
def create_item(name: str, price: float):
    return {"name": name, "price": price}

Run your app: 

uvicorn main:app --reload
Open http://localhost:8000/docs in your browser.

from flask import Flask
from specforge.flask import SpecForge

app = Flask(__name__)

# Mount SpecForge pointing to your OpenAPI JSON spec
SpecForge(app, spec_url="/api/spec.json", path="/docs")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(port=5000, debug=True)

Open http://localhost:5000/docs in your browser.

docs.title: 3. What You Get at /docs
docs.text:
Once you open the docs endpoint:

  1. Interactive API Explorer:
  2. Send requests with live header, query, and JSON body editors.
  3. Inspect response statuses, timing, headers, and formatted bodies.

  4. One-click cURL, Python (httpx), and JavaScript (fetch) snippet generators.

  5. Automated Schema Boundary Fuzzing:

  6. Switch to the Automated Tests section on any route.
  7. Run combinatorial boundary attacks against string lengths, numerical constraints, required fields, and formatting rules.

  8. Instantly uncover whether your API handles bad inputs cleanly or crashes with 500 Internal Server Error.

  9. Export to Pytest:

  10. Click Export Pytest to download a production-ready test file parametrized with every generated edge case.

docs.title: FastAPI Integration
docs.text: SpecForge is designed to be the ultimate companion for FastAPI. It seamlessly discovers FastAPI's native /openapi.json and injects an interactive workspace without altering your route logic or application state.

docs.title: Basic Mounting
docs.text:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from specforge import SpecForge

app = FastAPI(title="Payment Gateway API", version="1.0.0")

# Mount SpecForge
SpecForge(app)

By default, SpecForge: - Mounts at /docs. - Automatically fetches /openapi.json. - Disables FastAPI's default Swagger UI so you enjoy the full SpecForge studio.

docs.title: Customizing Configuration
docs.text:
You can customize the mounting path, spec URL, page title, and existing project tests:

from fastapi import FastAPI
from specforge import SpecForge

app = FastAPI()

SpecForge(
    app,
    path="/api-studio",                  # Custom URL path
    spec_url="/openapi.json",            # Custom spec location
    title="Payment Gateway Studio",      # Browser tab title
    theme="theme-2",                     # Default theme: theme-1 (Indigo), theme-2 (Emerald Teal), theme-3 (Dark), theme-4 (Cobalt)
    test_paths=["tests"],                # Index existing repository tests
    read_only=False,                     # Allow execution of requests and fuzzers
)

docs.title: Security & Production Hardening
docs.text:
In sensitive production environments, you can easily: - Restrict SpecForge to development environments. - Protect the documentation and test plan routes with FastAPI dependencies (e.g. API keys or OAuth2):

import os
from fastapi import FastAPI, Depends, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import HTTPBasic, HTTPBasicCredentials
from specforge import SpecForge

app = FastAPI()
security = HTTPBasic()

def verify_docs_admin(credentials: HTTPBasicCredentials = Depends(security)):
    expected_user = os.getenv("DOCS_ADMIN_USER", "admin")
    expected_pass = os.getenv("DOCS_ADMIN_PASSWORD")
    if not expected_pass or credentials.username != expected_user or credentials.password != expected_pass:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
            headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Basic"},
        )

env = os.getenv("ENVIRONMENT", "development")

if env == "development":
    # Mount without authentication in dev
    SpecForge(app)
elif env == "staging":
    # Mount with dependency protection and disabled raw fuzzing endpoints
    SpecForge(
        app,
        dependencies=[Depends(verify_docs_admin)],
        enable_api_endpoints=False,  # Disable /specforge/api/plan and /export-pytest
    )
else:
    # Disable docs entirely in production
    pass

docs.title: Flask Integration
docs.text: SpecForge integrates with Flask as a standard Blueprint, giving you the complete interactive API client, fuzzing engine, and existing test explorer.

docs.title: Basic Mounting
docs.text:
from flask import Flask, jsonify
from specforge.flask import SpecForge

app = Flask(__name__)

# Register SpecForge Blueprint
SpecForge(
    app,
    spec_url="/api/spec.json",    # Path to your OpenAPI JSON route
    path="/docs",                 # URL where SpecForge will be served
)

@app.route("/api/spec.json")
def get_spec():
    # Return your OpenAPI 3.0+ schema dictionary or loaded YAML
    return jsonify({
        "openapi": "3.0.0",
        "info": {"title": "Flask API", "version": "1.0.0"},
        "paths": {
            "/users": {
                "get": {
                    "summary": "List users",
                    "responses": {"200": {"description": "OK"}}
                }
            }
        }
    })

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(port=5000, debug=True)

docs.title: Configuration Options
docs.text:
When mounting on a Flask application:

Parameter Type Default Description app Flask Required Your Flask application instance. spec_url str "/openapi.json" Route where your OpenAPI JSON/YAML is accessible. path str "/docs" Route where the SpecForge studio HTML is mounted. title str "SpecForge - API Explorer & Quality Gate" HTML page title. theme str "theme-1" Initial UI color theme (theme-1, theme-2, theme-3, theme-4). test_paths list[str] None Directories or files to discover existing pytest/unittest suites.

docs.title: Existing Project Tests Integration
docs.text: Most production repositories already contain extensive test suites written in pytest or unittest. SpecForge can automatically index and display these tests in a dedicated Project Tests tab and link them directly to their corresponding API routes.

docs.title: Quick Setup
docs.text:
Pass test_paths when mounting SpecForge in your FastAPI or Flask app:

FastAPIFlask 
from fastapi import FastAPI
from specforge import SpecForge

app = FastAPI(title="Store API")

# Pass folder or specific test files
SpecForge(
    app,
    test_paths=["tests"],
)

from flask import Flask
from specforge.flask import SpecForge

app = Flask(__name__)

SpecForge(
    app,
    spec_url="/api/spec.json",
    test_paths=["tests"],
)

docs.title: What SpecForge Discovers
docs.text: When SpecForge mounts, it parses your test files statically (without executing arbitrary test code or fixtures) to extract: * Test Functions & Classes: Names, line numbers, and file paths. * Docstrings: Human-readable descriptions of what each test verifies. * Parameterized Matrices: Extracted @pytest.mark.parametrize argument sets. * Associated Route Endpoints: Automatically detected API routes.

docs.title: How Routes Are Linked
docs.text: SpecForge links your existing tests to OpenAPI routes using two mechanisms:

docs.title: 1. Automatic HTTP Client Detection (Zero Configuration)
docs.text:
If your test uses common test clients (client.get(...), httpx.post(...), requests.delete(...)), SpecForge automatically parses the endpoint string and binds the test to that route:

def test_create_user_underage(client):
    """Rejects registration when age is below legal requirement."""
    response = client.post("/users", json={"username": "bob", "age": 12})
    assert response.status_code == 422

In the API Explorer, /users will now proudly display:

🔗 Associated Project Tests: 1 (test_create_user_underage)

docs.title: 2. Explicit Annotation Marker
docs.text:
For complex test setups, you can explicitly link a test using a decorator comment or docstring:

def test_complex_billing_workflow(billing_fixture):
    """
    specforge: POST /billing/charge
    Verifies retry logic when third-party gateway responds with timeout.
    """
    ...

docs.title: Security & Isolation
docs.text:
• Zero Arbitrary Execution: Tests are discovered via Python's Abstract Syntax Tree (ast). SpecForge never runs unvetted test files during discovery.
  • Safe Path Traversal Protection: SpecForge ensures all scanned files reside strictly within permitted project directories.

docs.title: Schema Boundary Fuzzing
docs.text: SpecForge's core innovation is active quality verification. Rather than passively rendering API documentation, SpecForge algorithmically analyzes every JSON Schema rule on your endpoints and constructs targeted boundary test cases.

docs.title: The "Zero 500s" Invariant
docs.text:
In modern web development, clients send bad, missing, or malformed data all the time.

  • Good Behavior: The server catches the validation failure and returns a structured 400 Bad Request or 422 Unprocessable Entity.
  • Dangerous Behavior: The application crashes with an unhandled exception, leaking stack traces, creating log noise, and returning 500 Internal Server Error.

SpecForge runs automated boundary tests specifically to prove your API upholds the Zero 500s Invariant: no edge-case input should ever produce an unhandled server exception.

docs.title: Automated Fuzzing Strategies by Type
docs.text: SpecForge inspects parameter and request body schemas to synthesize edge cases:

docs.title: 1. String Fields
docs.text:
• Whitespace Only: Probes whether your backend strips strings (e.g. " "). Catches database errors when blank strings bypass min_length or unique constraints.
  • Empty String: Tests "" when a field is required or non-empty.
  • Length Boundaries: Exact min_length - 1 (underflow) and max_length + 1 (overflow).
  • Format Violations: Synthesizes invalid formats for email, uuid, date, date-time, and uri.
  • Dangerous Payloads: Checks for null-byte injection (\x00), Unicode 4-byte astral characters (emojis), and long strings.

docs.title: 2. Number & Integer Fields
docs.text:
• Boundaries: Generates values at minimum - 1 and maximum + 1.
  • Negative Values: Sends negative values against unsigned counters or prices.
  • Type Pollution: Injects floating-point decimals into strict integer fields.
  • Extreme Numbers: Tests standard integer overflow numbers (2^31 - 1, 2^63 - 1).

docs.title: 3. Object & Body Schemas
docs.text:
• Combinatorial Required Field Omission: Strips each required field one by one to verify the server returns clean field-level error messages.
  • Unexpected Keys (additionalProperties): Injects extra, undeclared fields to detect mass-assignment vulnerabilities.
  • Empty Payloads: Tests sending {} when fields are expected.

docs.title: 4. Array Fields
docs.text:
• Boundary Sizing: Probes minItems - 1 and maxItems + 1.
  • Duplicate Items: Injects duplicate items when uniqueItems: true is set.
  • Empty Arrays: Sends [] to test empty container validation.

docs.title: Running Boundary Tests in the UI
docs.text:
1. Open /docs in your browser.
  2. Select any operation in the left sidebar (e.g. POST /users).
  3. Scroll down to the Automated Contract Tests section.
  4. Click Run All Invariant Tests.
  5. SpecForge will execute the suite in real-time, displaying passing invariants in green and flagging any 500 Server Crashes in red with full cURL reproduction snippets!

docs.title: Pytest Exporter
docs.text:
Finding API bugs in an interactive client is great, but ensuring they don't regress in continuous integration is essential.

SpecForge bridges interactive discovery with automated CI pipelines via the One-Click Pytest Exporter.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: Whenever SpecForge plans or executes boundary tests for an endpoint, you can export those cases directly into valid, standalone Python test files.

docs.title: In the UI
docs.text: Inside the Automated Contract Tests panel of any endpoint, click the Export Pytest button. SpecForge will instantly generate and download a clean test_api_contracts.py file.

docs.title: Programmatically
docs.text:
You can also generate pytest code from your Python scripts or CI jobs using the PytestExporter:

from specforge.parser.openapi3 import OpenAPIParser
from specforge.testing.planner import TestPlanner
from specforge.testing.exporters.pytest_export import PytestExporter

# 1. Parse OpenAPI Spec
parser = OpenAPIParser(spec_dict)
spec = parser.parse()

# 2. Pick an operation and plan boundary tests
operation = spec.paths["/users"].operations["post"]
test_plan = TestPlanner.plan_operation_tests(operation)

# 3. Export to Pytest code
code = PytestExporter.export_operation_tests(
    test_plan=test_plan,
    base_url="http://localhost:8000"
)

# 4. Save to test directory
with open("tests/test_users_contracts.py", "w") as f:
    f.write(code)

docs.title: Sample Generated Pytest Code
docs.text:
The generated file is 100% standard pytest code using httpx and @pytest.mark.parametrize:

"""Automated Contract and Invariant Tests generated by SpecForge."""

import pytest
import httpx

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8000"

TEST_CASES = [
    {
        "id": "whitespace_username",
        "description": "Reject whitespace-only username",
        "payload": {"username": "   ", "age": 25},
        "expected_status": 422,
    },
    {
        "id": "missing_required_age",
        "description": "Reject payload when required field 'age' is missing",
        "payload": {"username": "alice"},
        "expected_status": 422,
    },
    {
        "id": "negative_age",
        "description": "Reject age below minimum 0",
        "payload": {"username": "alice", "age": -1},
        "expected_status": 422,
    },
]

@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", TEST_CASES, ids=lambda c: c["id"])
def test_post_users_invariants(case):
    """Enforce Zero 500s invariant against schema boundary violations."""
    with httpx.Client(base_url=BASE_URL, timeout=5.0) as client:
        response = client.post("/users", json=case["payload"])

        # Zero 500s Invariant: Must NEVER crash with 500
        assert response.status_code != 500, (
            f"Zero 500s Invariant Failed! Edge case '{case['description']}' "
            f"caused unhandled 500 crash."
        )
        assert response.status_code == case["expected_status"]
